question.text: The treatment of an aqueous solution of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>74</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Cu</mi><msub><mfenced><msub><mi>NO</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msub></math> with excess <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>KI</mi></math> results in a brown solution along with the formation of a precipitate. Passing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi></math> through this brown solution gives another precipitate <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math>. The amount of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math> (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math>) is____[Given: Atomic mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>39</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>Cu</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>63</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>127</mn></math>]
